disabled.title: Finance is not enabled
disabled.desc: The accounting module is switched off for this deployment.

forbidden.title: No access to finance
forbidden.desc: Ask an administrator for the accounting permission.

mode.label: Stripe environment
mode.testBanner: TEST MODE — you are viewing Stripe test data. Nothing here is real money.

reason.CODE_NOT_FOUND: Event code detected — no event with this code yet

agreement.title: Commercial agreement
agreement.help: How Bilit's commission is calculated for this event. Components add up; leave a value at 0 to not use it. Changing it later creates a new version — past sales keep the version they were booked with.
agreement.gross: Percentage of what the customer paid
agreement.net: Percentage of what the customer paid − Stripe fee
agreement.perTicketHint: Ticket count from Stripe metadata (default 1 per payment)
agreement.eventFeeHint: Charged once to the organiser when you post it
agreement.reverse: Refunds reverse the commission pro rata
agreement.added: Added on top of the ticket price (customer pays ticket + fee)

dashboard.title: Finance dashboard
dashboard.sub: Based on imported Stripe transactions and the accounting ledger. Each currency is shown separately — nothing is converted.
dashboard.emptyDesc: Connect Stripe and run a synchronisation to import transactions.
dashboard.asOfEnd: At the end of the period
dashboard.unallocatedHint: Stripe money not yet linked to an event
dashboard.attentionDesc: Some Stripe money is not yet assigned to an event or account.
dashboard.explain: Gross sales is what customers paid. Stripe fees are taken from Stripe's own balance transactions. Organiser payable = gross − refunds − Stripe fees (when the organiser bears them) − Bilit commission. Outstanding = payable − payments made. Payouts move money from Stripe to the bank and are never counted as sales.

tx.title: Stripe transactions
tx.sub: Every Stripe balance transaction, with gross, fee and net kept separately.
tx.search: Search ID, description or event code
tx.emptyDesc: Run a Stripe sync, or change the filters.

detail.title: Stripe transaction
detail.amountsSale: The whole sale: the payment plus every refund and dispute that belongs to it.
detail.ledgerDesc: Double-entry postings for this transaction, including reversals.
detail.unmatchDesc: The ledger posting is reversed and the money moves to unallocated receipts. Automatic matching will not reassign it.
detail.onTop: added on top of ticket price

match.title: Assign to event
match.desc: The ledger is re-posted (the previous posting is reversed, never edited) and the change is recorded in the audit log.
match.reasonHint: Required. Shown in the audit log.
match.overrideConfirm: I confirm this assignment despite the warning

events.title: Events
events.sub: Accounting events with their unique event code, organiser and commission agreement. Stripe payments are matched to events by code.
events.formDesc: The event code must be unique. Stripe payment descriptions or metadata containing it are matched to this event.
events.emptyDesc: Create an event and give it the code used in Stripe payment descriptions.
events.name: Name
events.codeHint: e.g. EVT-BER-2026-001 — letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore
events.organiserHint: Payments are only allocated once an organiser is linked
events.noOrganiserWarn: No organiser linked — payments stay unmatched
events.changeReasonHint: Required when the event already has transactions
events.profitDesc: From the ledger. Revenue, cash, Stripe fees, organiser payable and Bilit profit are separate concepts.
events.agreementsDesc: Every version is kept. Sales record the version used to calculate them.
events.newAgreementDesc: Applies to transactions imported or re-assigned from now on. Already-booked sales are not recalculated.
events.feePosted: Event fee charged to the organiser
events.onTop: added on top of ticket price

organisers.title: Organisers
organisers.sub: Accounting organisers are created here by an administrator — never automatically from Stripe customers.
organisers.formDesc: Bank details are encrypted and only shown after re-authentication.
organisers.search: Search name, company, email or ID
organisers.emptyDesc: Create an organiser, then link it to its events.
organisers.name: Name
organisers.bankHelp: Stored encrypted. Leave empty if unknown.
organisers.eventsDesc: Events belonging to this organiser. Stripe sales for these events count towards the organiser's balance.
organisers.statementDesc: Every booking that changes what Bilit owes this organiser, with a running balance.

payments.title: Organiser payments
payments.sub: Money Bilit paid to organisers. Each payment is its own ledger entry and reduces the outstanding balance; Stripe data is never changed.
payments.recordDesc: Records a payment from Bilit's bank account to the organiser.
payments.emptyDesc: Record payments as you make them so outstanding balances stay correct.
payments.eventHint: Optional — leave empty for a payment covering several events
payments.voidDesc: The payment is kept, marked VOIDED, and its ledger entry is reversed.

stripe.title: Stripe
stripe.sub: Connection, webhooks and synchronisation for the selected environment.

conn.title: Stripe integration — {mode}
conn.desc: Server-side API key, encrypted at rest. The key is never shown again or sent to the browser.
conn.keyDesc: Use a restricted key (recommended) with read access only.
conn.perms: Read: Balance, Balance transactions, Charges, PaymentIntents, Refunds, Disputes, Payouts. Optional write: Webhook endpoints (only to register the webhook automatically).
conn.disconnectDesc: The stored key and webhook secret are destroyed. Imported transactions and the ledger are kept.

webhook.title: Webhook
webhook.desc: Stripe notifies Bilit immediately; every event is signature-verified and processed once. A scheduled sync every 30 minutes covers any gap.
webhook.autoDesc: Creates the endpoint {url} in Stripe and stores its signing secret. Needs Webhook Endpoints write access.
webhook.manualDesc: From the Stripe Dashboard endpoint, or printed by `stripe listen` for local testing.

cli.title: Local development with the Stripe CLI
cli.desc: Production never depends on the CLI. For local testing, forward test-mode events to your machine and paste the whsec_ secret it prints into test mode.

log.title: Webhook events
log.desc: Received Stripe events. Payloads are not trusted: each one triggers a fresh fetch from the Stripe API.

security.title: Security
security.desc: Stripe credentials are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and never exposed to the browser, logs or API responses. Changing them requires re-authentication and is audited.

payouts.title: Payouts
payouts.sub: Transfers from the Stripe balance to Bilit's bank account. A payout is not a sale.

sync.title: Stripe sync
sync.sub: Import Stripe balance transactions and payouts in the background. Safe to run any number of times.
sync.idempotent: Running a sync twice never creates duplicate transactions or ledger entries.
sync.running: A run is in progress — this page refreshes automatically.
sync.errorsDesc: Already-processed transactions are kept; retry re-fetches only these.
sync.how: Stripe balance transactions are the source of truth: each one is imported once (unique Stripe ID), matched to an event by its code and posted to the ledger. A failing transaction is recorded and skipped without stopping the run; large imports resume from where they stopped.

recon.title: Reconciliation
recon.sub: Transactions that need attention, and a check of the ledger against Stripe.
recon.neverRun: Not run yet — it also runs after every sync.
recon.problemsDesc: {ledger} transaction(s) do not match their ledger posting; {charges} successful charge(s) have no balance transaction yet.
recon.stripeDiffNote: The difference to Stripe's balance is only expected to be zero after a full historical sync.
recon.queueDesc: No event code, unknown code, inactive event, no organiser, currency mismatch, duplicates or missing classification.

reports.title: Reports
reports.sub: Sales, event profitability and Stripe reconciliation. CSV exports use plain decimal amounts and open directly in Excel.

d.sales: One row per Stripe payment with its refunds and fees.
d.event-profit: One row per event and currency, from the ledger.
d.reconciliation: Every Stripe transaction with its accounting status.

more.statementDesc: Per organiser and currency, with CSV export.

ledger.title: Accounting ledger
ledger.sub: Double-entry journal. Entries are append-only: corrections are reversals, never edits or deletions.
ledger.reverseDesc: An equal and opposite entry is posted; the original stays in the ledger marked REVERSED.

adj.title: Manual adjustment
adj.desc: Posts a balanced entry in the {mode} mode books. Stripe transactions are never altered.

presets.organiserCharge: Charge organiser: organiser payable → Bilit fees
presets.organiserCredit: Credit organiser: other expenses → organiser payable

periods.title: Accounting periods
periods.desc: A closed month accepts no new postings (enforced by the database). Late Stripe activity is booked in the current open period with its original date kept. Reopening requires a reason and is audited.
periods.none: No closed periods — all months are open.

settings.title: Finance settings
settings.sub: How Stripe payments are matched to events, and accounting defaults.
settings.baseHint: For reporting; other currencies are never silently converted
settings.defaultModeHint: Which Stripe mode the finance screens open on
settings.qtyKeyHint: Used for per-ticket commission; default 1 per payment
settings.timezone: Posting dates use the organisation time zone ({tz}).
settings.rulesDesc: Tried in order. The first rule that finds a code which exists in Bilit wins; several different codes are never guessed.
settings.patternHint: First capture group is the code
settings.exactDesc: Matches any existing event code that appears as a word in the payment description.
settings.how: Put the event code in Stripe metadata (event_code) for new payments; keep the description rule for existing payments that only carry it in the description.

link.title: Link events to this organiser
link.desc: Choose the events this organiser runs. Detected codes become new events under this organiser, and their existing Stripe sales are matched straight away.
link.detectedDesc: Taken from payment descriptions (e.g. “for event: Blood In Blood Out Berlin (B41-0091)”). The name is the text before the code — edit it if needed.
link.noneDetected: No unlinked event codes found in Stripe.
link.name: Event name

import.title: Import events from Stripe transactions
import.desc: Event codes found in payment descriptions that have no event yet. The name is the text after “event:” and before the code. Their sales are matched as soon as the event exists and has an organiser.
import.none: No new event codes found in the imported transactions. Run a Stripe sync first.
import.name: Event name
import.organiserNote: Events without an organiser are created, but their sales stay unmatched until you link an organiser (from the event or organiser page).

fin.otherCurrency: Showing {c} activity booked to this {e} event.
fin.paidShare: Share of the amount due already paid

kpi.dueHint: After booking fee, refunds and deductions

flow.title: Where the money went
flow.desc: Customers paid → booking fee → organiser money → paid → remaining.
flow.deductionsHint: Fixed event fees and manual adjustments
flow.feeInRefunds: of which booking fee refunded (charged to organiser)

pl.title: Event profitability
pl.desc: Bilit's profit and loss for {event}, straight from the ledger.
pl.grossHint: Customer money; most of it belongs to the organiser
pl.bilitBorneHint: Where the agreement leaves the loss with Bilit

separation.title: Who the money belongs to
separation.desc: Ticket revenue, booking fee, organiser money and Bilit profit kept apart.

terms.title: Booking fee & commercial terms
terms.desc: Each change creates a new version. The booking fee can be re-applied to sales already booked.

fee.title: Change booking fee
fee.desc: The booking fee percentage for this event only.
fee.invalid: Enter a percentage between 0 and 100 with up to two decimals.
fee.apply: Re-apply to sales already booked to this event
fee.applyHelp: Every booked sale (and its refunds) is re-posted at the new rate: the old postings are reversed, never edited. Do this before settling with the organiser.
fee.futureHelp: Only sales imported or matched from now on use the new rate; booked sales keep the rate they were calculated with.

scopes.allHelp: Every booked sale (and its refunds) is re-posted at the new rate; old postings are reversed, never edited. Use before settling.
scopes.fromHelp: Sales made on or after this date use the new rate; earlier sales keep theirs (e.g. 7 % until yesterday, 10 % from today).
scopes.futureHelp: Booked sales keep the rate they were calculated with.

fee.basis: How the booking fee is charged

bases.ADDED: Added on top of the ticket price
bases.GROSS: Included — % of what the customer paid
bases.NET: Included — % of paid amount after Stripe fee

basisHelp.ADDED: Customer pays ticket + fee. €35 ticket + 10 % = €38.50 paid → booking fee €3.50, organiser €35.00.
basisHelp.GROSS: Fee is a share of the amount paid. €38.50 paid at 10 % → fee €3.85.
basisHelp.NET: Fee is a share of the amount paid after Stripe's fee.

basisShort.NET: of amount paid after Stripe fee

pay.title: Pay organiser
pay.desc: Settlement for {organiser}. The payment is recorded as its own ledger entry.
pay.overpay: This pays {v} more than is due (overpaid).

payEdit.title: Edit payment
payEdit.desc: Changing the amount, date, method or reference reverses the original ledger entry and posts a corrected one.

payDelete.title: Delete this payment?
payDelete.desc: Financial records never disappear: the payment is kept, marked VOIDED, and its ledger entry is reversed.

payments.title: Organiser payments
payments.desc: Every payment for this event, including edited and deleted (voided) ones.

tx.traceDesc: Each row is a Stripe transaction; open it to see the order, charge, fees and ledger postings.

exp.title: Expenses
exp.tabDesc: Platform costs for this event (venue, artist, marketing…). They reduce Bilit's profit and are never deducted from the organiser.
exp.desc: Recorded in the event currency and posted to the ledger.
exp.emptyDesc: Add venue, artist, marketing and other costs to see the event's true profit.
exp.name: Expense
exp.borneByHint: Who carries the cost. Organiser = deducted from their settlement.
exp.receiptHint: PDF, PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 10 MB
exp.receiptFailed: Saved, but the receipt upload failed
exp.deleteDesc: The expense is kept, marked as deleted, and its ledger entry is reversed.
exp.platformNote: Platform cost: reduces Bilit's profit on this event. It is not charged to or deducted from the organiser.

summary.title: Financial summary
summary.desc: Sales, booking fee, settlement and profit for this event.

sales.title: Sales report
sales.desc: Every order with refunds, Stripe fee and booking fee.

transactions.title: Stripe transactions
transactions.desc: All balance transactions booked to the event.

payments.title: Organiser payments
payments.desc: Payment history including edits and voids.

ledger.title: Ledger entries
ledger.desc: Double-entry postings tagged with this event.

statement.title: Organiser statement
statement.desc: Running balance of everything owed to and paid to the organiser.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.desc: Every financial change to this event, who made it and why.

events.title: Events — financials
events.sub: Every event with its sales, booking fee, organiser settlement and Bilit profit. Amounts are never mixed across currencies.

overview.title: Financial overview
overview.sub: All events: ticket sales, booking fees, organiser payments, expenses and Bilit profit.
overview.empty: No financial activity in this period
overview.emptyDesc: Choose a longer period or import Stripe transactions.
overview.outstandingHint: Due but not yet paid, as of the end of the period
overview.convertedNote: Indicative, at the rates in Finance settings. Never used for postings.
overview.missingRates: No rate set for {list}; those amounts are left out of the converted totals.
overview.none: No profit or loss booked in this period.

orgFin.title: Financial account
orgFin.expensesHint: Bilit's own costs on this organiser's events (not deducted from them)
orgFin.unassigned: Some payments are not tied to a specific event; they count towards the organiser's total but not to any single event.
orgFin.profitHint: Booking fees − Stripe fees and costs borne by Bilit

portalUsers.title: Organiser portal access
portalUsers.desc: Members who may see this organiser's own figures under “My finances”.
portalUsers.none: No one has portal access yet.
portalUsers.note: Portal users see only this organiser's live sales, booking fees, settlement and payments — never Bilit's profit, costs or other organisers. Invite the person under Members first (a Viewer role is enough).

portal.title: My finances
portal.sub: Sales, booking fees and payments for {name}.

fx.title: Reporting currency
fx.desc: Optional: show global totals converted into one currency.
fx.currencyHint: Leave empty to show each currency separately only
fx.note: Rates are indicative and used only for the converted overview. Every calculation and posting stays in the event's own currency.

fin.feeRecover: Booking fee to recover from organiser
fin.feeRecoverHint: Booking fee was refunded to customers. Under the platform policy the booking fee is non-refundable for Bilit, so this amount is charged to the organiser (already deducted from what they are due).

policy.title: Refund policy
policy.desc: How refunds affect Bilit's booking fee.
policy.nonRefundableHelp: Refunds never reduce Bilit's booking fee. If a booking fee is refunded to a customer, the organiser is charged for it (shown as “booking fee to recover from organiser”).
policy.note: Changing this re-calculates all existing refunds (old postings are reversed, never edited).

overview.title: Bookkeeping
overview.sub: Company books: income, costs, supplier invoices, VAT and payroll — every figure comes from the ledger.
overview.emptyDesc: Upload a supplier invoice or add an expense to get started.
overview.plDesc: All income and costs booked in {c} for the period.

doc.title: Invoices & expenses
doc.sub: Supplier invoices (to pay) and expenses (already paid). Upload the PDF or photo; every document is posted to the ledger.
doc.billDesc: A supplier invoice Bilit owes until it is paid.
doc.expenseDesc: A cost that has already been paid (card, bank, cash or by an employee).
doc.search: Search supplier, invoice no. or description
doc.eventHint: Optional — the cost then counts towards that event's profit
doc.fileHint: PDF, PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 15 MB
doc.fileFailed: Saved, but the file upload failed
doc.emptyDesc: Upload supplier invoices and add expenses; they are booked to the right cost account automatically.
doc.deleteDesc: The document is kept, marked as deleted, and its ledger entries are reversed.

emp.title: Employees
emp.sub: Staff on the payroll. Each employee has their own country and currency.
emp.desc: Personal and payroll details. Bank details are encrypted.
emp.forbidden: You need the payroll permission to see employees.
emp.emptyDesc: Add your staff to create payslips for them.
emp.name: Name

ps.title: Payslips
ps.sub: Enter pay and deductions from your accountant or payroll provider; the system works out net pay, year-to-date totals and issues the PDF.
ps.forbidden: You need the payroll permission to see payslips.
ps.desc: Amounts are entered by hand — nothing is calculated from tax tables.
ps.label: Description
ps.notesHint: Printed at the bottom of the PDF
ps.tooMuch: Deductions are larger than gross pay.
ps.manualNote: Check figures against your payroll provider. Issued payslips cannot be changed — void and reissue instead.
ps.noEmployeesDesc: Payslips are created for employees listed under Employees.
ps.emptyDesc: Create a payslip, check it as a draft PDF, then issue it.
ps.finaliseDesc: It gets a number, is booked to the ledger and the PDF is stored. It can no longer be edited.
ps.voidDesc: The payslip is kept, marked void, and its ledger entries are reversed. Issue a corrected payslip afterwards.

pay.title: Stripe payment
pay.desc: Everything Stripe reports about this payment: status, decline reason, risk check, card, refunds and disputes.

issue.disputedBody: The customer disputed this payment with their bank. Respond in the Stripe dashboard before the deadline.
issue.risk: Stripe flagged this payment as risky

refund.title: Refund payment
refund.desc: Refund {customer} through Stripe. The money goes back to the card used.
refund.ticketOnlySub: Platform policy: the booking fee ({fee}) is non-refundable and stays with Bilit.
refund.fullSub: The booking fee is refunded too — it is charged back to the organiser.
refund.customSub: Partial refund of a chosen amount.
refund.keepFee: Bilit keeps its booking fee (organiser bears the refund)
refund.noteHint: Kept with the refund and in the audit log
refund.confirmBody: {amount} will be refunded to the customer's card through Stripe. This cannot be undone.

list.title: Payments
list.sub: Every card payment in Stripe — including declined and pending ones that never reach the books — with the reason and risk.
list.search: Search customer, email, order or charge id
list.emptyDesc: Run a Stripe sync to import payments, including failed ones.

inv.title: Invoices & credit notes
inv.desc: Issue an invoice for the sale (or a VAT invoice with the customer's business details) and a credit note for each refund. Documents are numbered, stored and never changed.
inv.voidDesc: It stays on file marked void; you can then issue a corrected one with a new number.
inv.vatDesc: For a business customer: their (company) name and address are required; add their VAT number if they have one.
inv.plainDesc: A receipt-style invoice for the customer, from the Stripe payment details.
inv.immutable: Once issued the document cannot be edited — void it and issue a new one if something is wrong.
inv.listSub: Invoices, VAT invoices and credit notes issued to ticket buyers.
inv.listEmptyDesc: Issue them from a transaction (Transactions → open a sale).

invSettings.title: Invoices
invSettings.desc: Seller details and VAT treatment printed on customer invoices, VAT invoices and credit notes.
invSettings.feeVat: VAT rate on the booking fee (%)
invSettings.feeVatHint: Booking fees are charged VAT-inclusive at this rate

modes.AGENT: Sold as agent for the organiser (no Bilit VAT)

ticketModeHint.AGENT: The ticket price belongs to the organiser; the invoice says so.
ticketModeHint.INCLUDED: Use if Bilit itself sells the tickets.

invSettings.accountantNote: Confirm the VAT treatment with your accountant before issuing VAT invoices.

acc.title: Accountant pack & AI review
acc.desc: Everything your accountant needs for a period — PDF report plus CSVs (ledger, P&L, VAT, events & settlement, organiser payments, expenses, payroll, refunds, payouts, invoices) — and automatic checks for gaps.
acc.aiDisabled: Set up the AI accountant under Finance settings first
acc.packNote: The pack includes the latest AI review for the same period, if there is one. Exports need a recent sign-in.
acc.noIssues: No gaps found by the automatic checks.
acc.aiSetup: Add an OpenAI API key under Finance settings → AI accountant to have the books reviewed by an AI bookkeeper.
acc.aiDisclaimer: AI suggestions are a second pair of eyes, not professional advice — confirm anything important with your accountant.

ai.title: AI accountant (OpenAI)
ai.desc: An AI bookkeeper reviews each period for gaps, inconsistencies and things your accountant will ask about.
ai.enableHelp: Runs only when someone presses “Run AI accountant review” on the Reports page.
ai.keyHint: From platform.openai.com → API keys. Stored encrypted, never shown again.
ai.keySet: Key saved ({hint}). Enter a new one to replace it.
ai.modelHint: Any OpenAI chat model your key can use, e.g. gpt-4.1 or gpt-4o
ai.instructionsHint: Added to the review prompt (e.g. your VAT scheme, year end, things to focus on)
ai.instructionsPh: e.g. We are UK VAT registered on the standard scheme; year end 31 March. Pay particular attention to organiser balances.
ai.privacy: Only aggregated figures are sent to OpenAI (totals, events, categories, checks). Customer names, emails and card details are never sent; employees are referred to by employee number only.
